correctness.rationale: The graph and face predicate are fully specified. Exhaustive enumeration finds exactly 20,651 faces, and a deterministic 10,319-pair discrete-Morse matching leaves one 0-cell, ten 5-cells, two 6-cells. An exact directed topological sort of all 120,222 nonempty cover relations proves acyclicity. Signed integral elimination gives the 10-by-2 differential whose columns are opposite primitive vectors with unit entries; its one nonzero elementary divisor is 1. With no intervening low-dimensional cells, the 5-skeleton is a wedge of 10 five-spheres and Hurewicz identifies attaching maps with these integer columns; a primitive cancellation leaves 9 five-spheres and one trivially attached six-sphere. An independent full mod-two boundary computation corroborates the ranks but is not substituted for the integral proof. All limits are finite and explicit.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The Pappus Levi graph is a three-regular, eighteen-vertex bipartite incidence graph and not a tree, cycle, complete multipartite graph, fully whiskered graph, or a block graph. A theorem about any of those restricted graph classes cannot be instantiated to it merely by using the same independence parameter. No encompassing published theorem implying this precise mixed-dimensional integral homotopy type was located.

value.rationale: For a canonical nonchordal eighteen-vertex incidence graph, the first higher-independence complex is a motivated and natural topological invariant extending the ordinary independence and tree/chordal literature. Its exact integral mixed-dimensional homotopy type, wedge^9 S5 plus S6, is unexpected from the nonpure dimension-nine face structure and is a useful fully reproducible benchmark for higher-independence topology. No general downstream theorem is claimed or required. The value does not rest on a fabricated first-ever assertion, routine adjacency counting, or negligible numeric improvement.
